- CP: N or S? The path only reads system prompt; no durable memory. Single stateless chat → N.

- ES: HelperBot tools are listed but not executed; the path uses no tools. Extension surface... tools are name-only declarations, fixed allowlist. Path doesn't invoke extensions → N (no dynamic extension on the path).

CVSS: AV:N (loopback bind by default documented deployment... documented default deployment is Docker publishing on 127.0.0.1; attacker is the party sending chat message — remote attacker via network once ports reachable. Documented default: loopback, so AV:L? Documented deployment publishes on 127.0.0.1, meaning attacker needs local access or user's browser (CORS * allows drive-by). Hmm. Attack vector: attacker sends POST to loopback — that's local. But CORS * allows a web page in operator's browser to do it (UI: Passive). Standard scoring for loopback-bound: AV:L/N? Actually network-reachable via the operator's browser = Adjacent? I'll go AV:N since HTTP API, UI:N, PR:N (no auth), AC:L, AT:N. Given the documented default binds 127.0.0.1, AV:L might be more accurate; but the target is a network service; the briefing says entry point "chat message ... no authentication" with precondition "network access to the agent port." I'll use AV:N.

Attacker doesn't own asset already — external user with network access.
